verses.zh: 耶路・巴力就是基甸，他和一切跟随的人早晨起来，在哈律泉旁安营。米甸营在他们北边的平原，靠近摩利冈。
verses.en: Jerub Baal (that is, Gideon) and his men[NOTE:1] got up the next morning and camped near the spring of Harod.[NOTE:2] The Midianites[NOTE:3] were camped north of them near the hill of Moreh in the valley.
notes: Heb “and all the people who were with him.”
The name Harod means, ironically, “trembling.”
Heb “Midian.” The LXX reads “and Amalek” (cf. v. 12; 6:33).
verses.commentary:
7:1 "Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon)" See note at
Jdgs. 6:32.

▣ "the spring of Harod" This name (BDB 353) means "trembling" (cf. Jdgs. 7:3). The valley of Jezreel
or Esdraelon is the geographical setting.

▣ "Midian" The LXX (Alexandrinus) adds "and Amalek" (from Jdgs. 6:33), both here and 7:12, but LXX
(Vaticanus) has only "Amalek" at Jdgs. 7:12.

▣ "the hill of Moreh" This is located to the southeast of Mt. Tabor (see The Macmillan Bible Atlas, p. 15,
maps 8, 60).

This is not the same locality as "the oak of Moreh" (Gen. 12:6; Deut. 11:30), which is near Shechem.

The name (BDB 435 II) means "teacher." Trees were sacred sites in the ANE, probably because they
identified in-ground water sources.

verses.zh: 耶和华对基甸说：「跟随你的人过多，我不能将米甸人交在他们手中，免得以色列人向我夸大，说：『是我们自己的手救了我们。』
verses.en: The Lord said to Gideon, “You have too many men for me to hand Midian over to you.[NOTE:1] Israel might brag,[NOTE:2] ‘Our own strength has delivered us.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the people who are with you are too numerous for me to give Midian into their hand.”
Heb “might glorify itself against me.”
Heb “my hand has delivered me.”
verses.commentary:
7:2 "The people who are with you are too many" God's ways are not man's way (cf. Isa. 55:6-9)!

▣ "for Israel would become boastful" God wanted all to know it was His victory, not Israel's
(cf. Deut. 8:17-18).

verses.zh: 现在你要向这些人宣告说：『凡惧怕胆怯的，可以离开基列山回去。』」于是有二万二千人回去，只剩下一万。
verses.en: Now, announce to the men,[NOTE:1] ‘Whoever is shaking with fear[NOTE:2] may turn around and leave Mount Gilead.’”[NOTE:3] Twenty-two thousand men[NOTE:4] went home;[NOTE:5] 10,000 remained.
notes: Heb “call into the ears of the people.”
Heb “afraid and shaking.”

Many interpreters reject the MT reading “and leave Mount Gilead” for geographical reasons. A possible alternative, involving rather radical emendation of the Hebrew text, would be, “So Gideon tested them” (i.e., thinned the ranks in this manner).
Heb “people.” The translation uses “men” because warriors are in view, and in ancient Israelite culture these would be only males. (This is also the case in vv. 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.)
Or “turned around, back.”
verses.commentary:
7:3 "Whoever is afraid and trembling" Lack of faith in God could cause panic to spread within the troops
(cf. Deut. 20:8).

Notice YHWH reduces the army of Gideon in two ways.

- those who are afraid, go home (22,000 reduced to 10,000)

- those who drink without watching (Jdgs. 7:5-8), go home; the group left would have been the best soldiers
(10,000 down to 3,000)

▣ "depart from Mount Gilead" This seems to be an early scribal error for Mt. Gilboa. Mt. Gilead is on
the eastern side of the Jordan, while Mt. Gilboa is in the plain of Esdraelon.

The UBS Text Project gives "Gilead" an "A" rating (certain). However, it does not fit the context.
Context is crucial and determines word meaning.

- Gilead ‒ גלעד

- Gilboa ‒ גלבע

The REB has "Mount Galud," from LXX, "Mount Galaad," which is a spring at the foot of Mt. Gilboa.

▣ "depart" This VERB (BDB 861, KB 1050, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense) occurs only here.

There are several options.

- NKJV ‒ "let him depart at once from Mt. Gilead"

- NJB, Peshitta ‒ "go back and watch from Mt. Gilboa"

- JPSOA ‒ "as a bird flies from Mt. Gilead"

- REB ‒ "to leave Mt. Galud at once"

- LXX (B) ‒ "leave Mt. Galaad"

- Kimchi ‒ "depart early" (Young's literal)

- G. F. Moore (ICC) ‒ "Gideon put them to the test" (BDB 861, #2; NAB)

- C. F. Burney ‒ "decamp"

Obviously no one knows. JPSOA marks this as "meaning of Heb. uncertain."

verses.zh: 耶和华对基甸说：「人还是过多；你要带他们下到水旁，我好在那里为你试试他们。我指点谁说：『这人可以同你去』，他就可以同你去；我指点谁说：『这人不可同你去』，他就不可同你去。」
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Gideon again, “There are still too many men.[NOTE:1] Bring them down to the water, and I will thin the ranks some more.[NOTE:2] When I say, ‘This one should go with you,’ pick him to go;[NOTE:3] when I say,[NOTE:4] ‘This one should not go with you,’ do not take him.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “too many people.”
Heb “test them for you there.”
Heb “he should go with you.”
Heb also has “about anyone to you.”
Heb “he should not go.”
verses.commentary:
7:4 "I will test them" YHWH Himself "tests" (BDB 864, KB 1057, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense). This term is from metallurgy and means to heat something to purify it
(i.e., smelter; cf. Isa. 48:10; Zech. 13:9). In this context it refers to YHWH trying human's hearts (cf. Ps. 17:3; 26:2; 66:10;
105:19; 1 Pet. 1:7).

verses.zh: 基甸就带他们下到水旁。耶和华对基甸说：「凡用舌头舔水，像狗舔的，要使他单站在一处；凡跪下喝水的，也要使他单站在一处。」
verses.en: So he brought the men[NOTE:1] down to the water. Then the Lord said to Gideon, “Separate those who lap the water as a dog laps from those who kneel to drink.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the people.”
Heb “Everyone who laps with his tongue from the water, as a dog laps, put him by himself, as well as the one who gets down on his knees to drink.”
verses.commentary:
7:5 "he brought the people down to the water" Josephus (Antiq. 5.6.3) tells us it was at noon when they
were very thirsty.

▣ "everyone who laps the water. . .everyone who kneels to drink" There are two opinions about these
different drinkers.

I tend to see the smaller group as the most inexperienced soldiers. YHWH brings victory through the
least likely group in order to show His power (cf. Jdgs. 7:2). It seems the former group was alert and prepared, while the
latter group was concerned more with their immediate physical needs. Josephus says the first group were cowards
(Antiq. 5.6.3) and the Jewish Study Bible agrees (p. 525).

Jewish tradition says that those who knelt showed they had at some point worshiped Ba'al (see Jewish
Study Bible, p. 525).

verses.zh: 于是用手捧着舔水的有三百人，其余的都跪下喝水。
verses.en: Only 300 men lapped with their hands to their mouths;[NOTE:1] the rest of the men[NOTE:2] kneeled to drink water.
notes: The Hebrew phrase, “with their hands to their mouths.” is difficult in light of v. 5, which distinguishes between dog-like lappers (who would not use their hands to drink) and those who kneel (who would presumably use their hands). The words “with their hands to their mouths” may have been misplaced. They fit better at the end of v. 5 or v. 6. Perhaps these words were originally a marginal scribal note which was later accidentally inserted into the text in the wrong place. But on the other hand since the 300 men were the men selected for the army, lapping with their hands to their mouth would allow them to see their surroundings which would be a good procedure for a soldier. The kneelers were sent away presumably because they made themselves more vulnerable to enemy attack.
Heb “the people.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对基甸说：「我要用这舔水的三百人拯救你们，将米甸人交在你手中；其余的人都可以各归各处去。」
verses.en: The Lord said to Gideon, “With the 300 men who lapped I will deliver the whole army,[NOTE:1] and I will hand Midian over to you.[NOTE:2] The rest of the men should go home.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you.” The Hebrew pronoun is masculine plural, probably referring to the entire army.
The Hebrew pronoun here is singular.
Heb “All the people should go, each to his place.”

verses.zh: 这三百人就带着食物和角；其余的以色列人，基甸都打发他们各归各的帐棚，只留下这三百人。米甸营在他下边的平原里。
verses.en: The men[NOTE:1] who were chosen[NOTE:2] took supplies[NOTE:3] and their trumpets. Gideon[NOTE:4] sent all the men of Israel back to their homes;[NOTE:5] he kept only 300 men. Now the Midianites[NOTE:6] were camped down below[NOTE:7] in the valley.
notes: Heb “The people.”
The words “who were chosen” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
The Hebrew text has “in their hands.”
Heb “he”; the referent (Gideon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “tents.”
Heb “Midian.”
The Hebrew text adds “him” (i.e., Gideon).
verses.commentary:
7:8 "provision" This term (BDB 845) usually means "food supply" (i.e., Jos. 1:11; 9:11), but here it seems
to refer to the empty food jars used to conceal the torches in the nighttime surprise attack.

It could also refer to the "trumpets." Not every person would normally have a trumpet but the
remaining 300 each had one.

▣ "each to his tent" This is a Hebrew idiom for "return home." It does not imply anything about what kind
of structure (cf. 1 Sam. 4:10; 13:2; 2 Sam. 18:17; 19:8; 20:1, 22).

verses.zh: 当那夜，耶和华吩咐基甸说：「起来，下到米甸营里去，因我已将他们交在你手中。
verses.en: That night the Lord said to Gideon,[NOTE:1] “Get up! Attack[NOTE:2] the camp, for I am handing it over to you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (Gideon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Go down against.”
The Hebrew verbal form is a perfect, emphasizing the certainty of the promise.
verses.commentary:
7:9-14 Gideon's tendency toward doubt is revealed again and dealt with by God again (i.e., a sign, cf.
Jdgs. 6:17, 36-40).

7:9 Notice YHWH reveals Himself in two dreams.

- Gideon's in Jdgs. 7:9

- a man in Jdgs. 7:13 (i.e., one of the enemy); God uses many ways to accomplish His will

▣ "for I have given it into your hands" This is a PROPHETIC PERFECT. This victory has
not yet occurred but YHWH's promise was certain.

verses.zh: 倘若你怕下去，就带你的仆人普拉下到那营里去。
verses.en: But if you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp with Purah your servant
verses.commentary: 7:10 "Purah your servant" This is obviously an eyewitness account!

verses.zh: 你必听见他们所说的，然后你就有胆量下去攻营。」于是基甸带着仆人普拉下到营旁。
verses.en: and listen to what they are saying. Then you will be brave[NOTE:1] and attack the camp.” So he went down with Purah his servant to where the sentries were guarding the camp.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your hands will be strengthened.”
Heb “to the edge of the ones in battle array who were in the camp.”

verses.zh: 米甸人、亚玛力人，和一切东方人都布散在平原，如同蝗虫那样多。他们的骆驼无数，多如海边的沙。
verses.en: Now the Midianites, Amalekites, and the people from the east covered the valley like a swarm of locusts.[NOTE:1] Their camels could not be counted; they were as innumerable as the sand on the seashore.
notes: Heb “Midian, Amalek, and the sons of the east were falling in the valley like locusts in great number.”
verses.commentary:
7:12 There are three groups of invaders identified (cf. Jdgs. 6:3): (1) Midianites, (2) Amalekites, (3) "all the sons
of the east."

▣ Notice the three ways the opposing army is characterized.

- as numerous as locusts

- camels without number

- as numerous as the sand on the seashore

It was a large coalition. No wonder Gideon was shocked to be told to reduce his 33,000 soldiers to 300!
This is the faith element in Israel's battles (cf. Deut. 3:22; 7:18; 20:1; 31:6, 8; 1 Sam. 17:45, 47; Ps. 20:7; 33:6-17; 44:1-3,
5-7; Isa. 63:1-6,9). YHWH was their covenant God and Divine Warrior (NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 545-549)!

verses.zh: 基甸到了，就听见一人将梦告诉同伴说：「我做了一梦，梦见一个大麦饼滚入米甸营中，到了帐幕，将帐幕撞倒，帐幕就翻转倾覆了。」
verses.en: When Gideon arrived, he heard a man telling another man about a dream he had.[NOTE:1] The man[NOTE:2] said, “Look! I had a dream. I saw[NOTE:3] a stale cake of barley bread rolling into the Midianite camp. It hit a tent so hard it knocked it over and turned it upside down. The tent just collapsed.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “And Gideon came, and, look, a man was relating to his friend a dream.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the man mentioned in the previous clause) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Look!” The repetition of this interjection, while emphatic in Hebrew, would be redundant in the English translation.
Heb “It came to the tent and struck it and it fell. It turned it upside down and the tent fell.”
verses.commentary:
7:13 "loaf of barley bread" This was food for the poor. The Hebrew word "loaf" (BDB 853) occurs only here
in the OT. The New Jerusalem Bible's footnote and Jewish Study Bible (p. 526) both say the "barley loaf" represented
the agricultural Israelites, while the "tent" represented the nomadic enemy.

verses.zh: 那同伴说：「这不是别的，乃是以色列人约阿施的儿子基甸的刀；　神已将米甸和全军都交在他的手中。」
verses.en: The other man said,[NOTE:1] “Without a doubt this symbolizes[NOTE:2] the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God is handing Midian and all the army over to him.”
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
Heb “This can be nothing but.”
verses.commentary:
7:14 This interpretation by another enemy soldier is also a revelation from YHWH. There is no reason why
an army as large as the one described (Jdgs. 7:12) should be afraid of Gideon and his much weaker troops.

YHWH has placed fear in the hearts of the enemy (cf. Jdgs. 7:22).

verses.zh: 基甸听见这梦和梦的讲解，就敬拜　神，回到以色列营中，说：「起来吧！耶和华已将米甸的军队交在你们手中了。」
verses.en: When Gideon heard the report of the dream and its interpretation, he praised God.[NOTE:1] Then he went back to the Israelite camp and said, “Get up, for the Lord is handing the Midianite army over to you!”
notes: Heb “he bowed down” or “worshiped.”
verses.commentary:
7:15 "its interpretation" This NOUN (BDB 991 I) used in this sense (i.e., "breaking" a
dream's meaning) is found only here.

▣ "he bowed in worship" Gideon has a worshipful moment amidst the enemy's camp!

verses.zh: 于是基甸将三百人分作三队，把角和空瓶交在各人手里（瓶内都藏着火把），
verses.en: He divided the 300 men into three units.[NOTE:1] He gave them all trumpets and empty jars with torches inside them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “heads.”

They hid the torches inside the earthenware jars to disguise their approach and to keep the torches from being extinguished by the breeze.tn Heb “the jars.” The noun has been replaced by the pronoun (“them”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
7:16 Torches will not burn in an overturned pottery jar. The jar had some hole in it or this is another
miracle of God!

verses.zh: 吩咐他们说：「你们要看我行事：我到了营的旁边怎样行，你们也要怎样行。
verses.en: He said to them, “Watch me and do as I do. Watch closely![NOTE:1] I am going to the edge of the camp. Do as I do!
notes: Or “look.”

verses.zh: 我和一切跟随我的人吹角的时候，你们也要在营的四围吹角，喊叫说：『耶和华和基甸的刀！』」
verses.en: When I and all who are with me blow our trumpets, you also blow your trumpets all around the camp. Then say, ‘For the Lord and for Gideon!’”
verses.commentary:
7:18 The war cry of Jdgs. 7:18 leaves out "a sword for" (see Peshitta) but the full form appears in Jdgs. 7:20.

This war cry (Jdgs. 7:18, 20) was the only part of the battle required of Gideon's soldiers. YHWH, as
the Divine Warrior (i.e., Holy War), is the victor!

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 526, supports this by noting that Gideon's soldiers had both hands full (i.e.,
jar and torch), so no hand for the sword. The sword was YHWH's sword! However, there is the question of how they also
carry a trumpet.

verses.zh: 基甸和跟随他的一百人，在三更之初才换更的时候，来到营旁，就吹角，打破手中的瓶。
verses.en: Gideon took 100 men to the edge of the camp[NOTE:1] at the beginning of the middle watch, just after they had changed the guards. They blew their trumpets and broke the jars they were carrying.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Gideon went, along with the 100 men who were with him, to the edge of the camp.”
Heb “that were in their hands.”
verses.commentary:
7:19 "middle watch" This was the second night watch from 10:00 pm to 2:00 am.

▣ "when they had just posted the watch" The Hebrew text has an intensified form here (i.e., an
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a PERFECT VERB from the same root, BDB 877,
KB 1086). Exactly why is uncertain. Apparently the guards were not yet settled in for their watch, while the other
guards were walking back to their tents.

▣ "trumpets" They used ram's horns.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

verses.zh: 三队的人就都吹角，打破瓶子，左手拿着火把，右手拿着角，喊叫说：「耶和华和基甸的刀！」
verses.en: All three units blew their trumpets and broke their jars. They held the torches in their left hand and the trumpets in their right.[NOTE:1] Then they yelled, “A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!”
notes: The Hebrew text adds, “in order to blow [them].” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary: 7:20 "A sword for the Lord and for Gideon" This was their battle cry!

verses.zh: 他们在营的四围各站各的地方；全营的人都乱窜。三百人呐喊，使他们逃跑。
verses.en: They stood in order[NOTE:1] all around the camp. The whole Midianite[NOTE:2] army ran away; they shouted as they scrambled away.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “each in his place.”
“Midianite” has been supplied here for clarity.
Or “fled.”
verses.commentary:
7:21 "crying out" This VERB (BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil IMPERFECT
with waw) is the opposite of the war cry of Gideon's army in Jdgs. 7:18 and 20. This VERB is
never used for victory, only the sound of fear, defeat, and flight (i.e., Micah 4:9).

There is another word for "crying out" (BDB 858, KB 1042) used in Jdgs. 7:23, for Gideon calling out
to the other Israeli tribes.

verses.zh: 三百人就吹角，耶和华使全营的人用刀互相击杀，逃到西利拉的伯・哈示他，直逃到靠近他巴的亚伯・米何拉。
verses.en: When the 300 men blew their trumpets, the Lord caused the Midianites to attack one another with their swords[NOTE:1] throughout[NOTE:2] the camp. The army fled to Beth Shittah on the way to Zererah. They went[NOTE:3] to the border of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.
notes: Heb “the Lord set the sword of each one against his friend.”
MT has “and throughout the camp,” but the conjunction (“and”) is due to dittography and should be dropped. Compare the ancient versions, which lack the conjunction here.
The words “they went” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
7:22 "the Lord set the sword of one against another" This is also mentioned
in 1 Sam. 14:20; 2 Chr. 20:23.

▣ "Beth-shittah" This location is uncertain. The name (BDB 112) means "house of Acacia. It is not the
same as "Shittim."

▣ "Abel-meholah" It means "dancing brook" (KB 7). This is located very close to the Jordan River, about
level with Samaria (cf. 1 Kgs. 4:12; 19:16).

verses.zh: 以色列人就从拿弗他利、亚设，和玛拿西全地聚集来追赶米甸人。
verses.en: Israelites from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh answered the call and chased the Midianites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Midian.”

verses.zh: 基甸打发人走遍以法莲山地，说：「你们下来攻击米甸人，争先把守约旦河的渡口，直到伯・巴拉。」于是以法莲的众人聚集，把守约旦河的渡口，直到伯・巴拉，
verses.en: Now Gideon sent messengers throughout the Ephraimite hill country who announced, “Go down and head off the Midianites.[NOTE:1] Take control of the fords of the streams[NOTE:2] all the way to Beth Barah and the Jordan River.”[NOTE:3] When all the Ephraimites had assembled,[NOTE:4] they took control of the fords[NOTE:5] all the way to Beth Barah and the Jordan River.
notes: Heb “to meet Midian.”
Heb “capture before them the waters.”
The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for clarification (also later in this verse).
Heb “And all the men of Ephraim were summoned.”
Heb “they captured the waters.”
verses.commentary:
7:24 The Ephramites are invited by Gideon to join in the pursuit of the invaders, especially at
the fords of the Jordan. This was so that several tribes could be part of the victory.

- Manasseh, Asher, Zebulon, Naphtali (Jdgs. 6:35)

- Ephraim (Jdgs. 7:24; 8:1); they cut off the enemy's retreat towards the fords of Jordan

▣ "Beth-barah" This name means, "house of the ford" (BDB 111). Its location is uncertain but
must be close to the Jordan (cf. Jdgs. 3:28).

verses.zh: 捉住了米甸人的两个首领：一名俄立，一名西伊伯；将俄立杀在俄立磐石上，将西伊伯杀在西伊伯酒榨那里；又追赶米甸人，将俄立和西伊伯的首级带过约旦河，到基甸那里。
verses.en: They captured the two Midianite generals, Oreb and Zeeb.[NOTE:1] They executed Oreb on the rock of Oreb and Zeeb[NOTE:2] in the winepress of Zeeb. They chased the Midianites[NOTE:3] and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon, who was now on the other side of the Jordan River.[NOTE:4]
notes: The names Oreb and Zeeb, which mean “Raven” and “Wolf” respectively, are appropriate because the Midianites had been like scavengers and predators to Israel.
The Hebrew text repeats the verb “executed.” This has not been repeated in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “Midian.”
Heb “beyond the Jordan.” The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text but has been supplied in the translation for clarity (also in 8:4).
verses.commentary:
7:25 "Oreb" This word means "raven" (BDB 788).

▣ "Zeeb" The word means "wolf" (BDB 255 II).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How does Jdgs. 7:2 explain the rest of the chapter?

- There are two options of how the soldiers drank and what it meant. Which one do you think is correct?

- How does Jdgs. 7:10 characterize Gideon?

- How did God defeat the invaders?

- Why was Ephraim invited to participate?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- YHWH must limit Gideon's army to show His power (cf. Jdgs. 7:2).

- Gideon is still afraid and must have yet another sign (cf. Jdgs. 7:9-14).

- Judges 7:24-25 shows how geographical places in Canaan, after the invasion of Israel, got their names.

- Gideon, like Samson, clearly shows the fallen, frail nature of Israel's judges/deliverers. YHWH's will and Spirit are the
true forces behind the historical events. YHWH uses fallen, weak people (i.e., Noah, Jacob, Moses) to accomplish His
purposes.
